units.subject: Well-being
units.title: Clean hands, healthy me
units.caps: National Curriculum Framework for Children from Birth to Four (2015), Early Learning and Development Area 1: Well-being (children are healthy and have a sense of good hygiene)
units.intention: Today I am learning how to keep my hands clean.

lesson.say: Germs are so tiny that we cannot see them. Germs on our hands can make us sick.
lesson.html:
🦠 👐

Germs are so tiny that we cannot see them. Germs on our hands can make us sick.

lesson.say: Wet your hands. Rub them with soap. Rinse them with water. Dry them on a clean towel.
lesson.html:
💧 🧼 🚿 🧻

  1. Wet your hands.
  2. Rub them with soap.
  3. Rinse with water.
  4. Dry them on a clean towel.

lesson.say: We wash our hands before we eat, after we use the toilet, and after we play outside.
lesson.html:
🍽️ 🚽 ⚽

We wash our hands before we eat, after the toilet and after playing outside.

example.q: Thando played in the sand. Now it is time to eat. What must he do first?
steps: There may be germs on his hands.
He must wash his hands before he eats.

questions.q: What do we use to wash our hands?
hints: We use it in the bathroom.
Soap and water wash germs away.
questions.explain: Soap and water wash the germs off our hands.

questions.q: When must we wash our hands?
hints: We always wash after the toilet.
questions.explain: We wash our hands after the toilet, so we do not spread germs.

questions.q: Put the hand washing steps in order.
hints: The soap comes after the water.
questions.explain: Wet, soap, rinse, dry.

questions.q: Lebo is going to eat an apple. What should she do first?
hints: Before eating, we make our hands clean.
questions.explain: Lebo washes her hands before she eats.

questions.q: Can we see germs?
hints: Can you see them on your hands?
They are too small to see.
questions.explain: Germs are too tiny to see. That is why we wash even when our hands look clean.

units.parent: Your child learned the steps for washing hands and when to wash them.
units.teacher: Shows whether the child can sequence a familiar self-care routine and link it to everyday moments.
units.done: Clean hands help everyone stay healthy.

units.subject: Well-being
units.title: Safe or not safe?
units.caps: National Curriculum Framework for Children from Birth to Four (2015), Early Learning and Development Area 1: Well-being (children build a sense of safety and security; identify dangerous objects and situations)
units.intention: Today I am learning which things are safe to touch.
units.prompt: How do you know it is not safe?

lesson.say: Some things can hurt us. Hot things, sharp things and medicine are not for playing.
lesson.html:
🔥 🔪 💊

Some things can hurt us: hot things, sharp things and medicine. They are not for playing.

lesson.say: If you see something that is not safe, do not touch it. Tell a grown-up.
lesson.html:
✋ 🧑

If you see something that is not safe, stop. Do not touch it. Tell a grown-up.

lesson.say: If you get lost, stay where you are and tell a safe grown-up your name.
lesson.html:
🧒 💬 👮

If you get lost, stay where you are. Tell a safe grown-up, like a police officer or a teacher, your name.

example.q: Sipho sees a box of matches on the table. What should he do?
steps: Fire is hot and can hurt.
Sipho should not touch them. He should tell a grown-up.

questions.q: Which one is safe to play with?
hints: Knives are sharp and fire is hot.
questions.explain: A ball is safe to play with. Knives and fire can hurt us.

questions.q: You see pills on the floor. What do you do?
hints: Medicine can make us sick if it is not for us.
A grown-up will know what to do.
questions.explain: Medicine is only for grown-ups to give. Tell a grown-up.

questions.q: Sort these into safe and not safe to touch.
hints: A hot pot burns and scissors are sharp.
questions.explain: A teddy and a book are safe. A hot pot and scissors can hurt us.

questions.q: You are lost at the shops. What should you do?
options: Stay and tell a safe grown-up
hints: Running makes it harder to find you.
Stay where you are and ask a shop worker or police officer.
questions.explain: Stay where you are and tell a safe grown-up your name.

questions.q: Why do we not touch the stove?
hints: We cook food on the stove.
It is hot and can burn.
questions.explain: The stove is hot. It can burn us.

units.parent: Your child talked about dangerous objects and what to do when lost. You could practise saying their full name and your phone number together.
units.teacher: Shows whether the child can tell safe from unsafe objects and names a help-seeking action.
units.done: When something is not safe, stop and tell a grown-up.

units.subject: Identity and Belonging
units.title: All about me
units.topic: Me and what I can do
units.caps: National Curriculum Framework for Children from Birth to Four (2015), Early Learning and Development Area 2: Identity and Belonging (children are aware of themselves as capable and confident learners; celebrating differences)
units.intention: Today I am thinking about me and the things I can do.
units.prompt: What can you do now that you could not do before?

lesson.say: There is only one you. Your name, your face and the things you like make you special.
lesson.html:
🧒 ⭐

There is only one you. Your name, your face and the things you like make you special.

lesson.say: You can do so many things. You can jump, sing, draw and help.
lesson.html:
🦘 🎤 🖍️ 🤝

You can do so many things: jump, sing, draw and help. Every day you learn something new.

lesson.say: People are different. Some are tall, some are short. We all belong.
lesson.html:
🧍🏾 🧍🏻 🧑🏽‍🦽 🧍🏿

People are different. Some are tall and some are short. Some walk and some use a wheelchair. We all belong.

example.q: Amahle says, "I can put on my shoes by myself!" How does she feel?
steps: Amahle learned to do something new.

questions.q: Which one is something you can do with your feet?
hints: Feet are at the bottom of your legs.
We clap with hands and listen with ears.
questions.explain: We jump with our feet.

questions.q: Zola wears glasses and Ben does not. What is true?
questions.explain: People can be different and still be friends.

questions.q: You learned to ride a bike. How might you feel?
hints: It was hard, but you did it.
questions.explain: We feel proud when we learn to do something new.

questions.q: Which is the same for all children?
options: We all wear the same shoes
We all like the same colour
hints: Shoes and colours are different for different people.
Everyone feels happy or sad sometimes.
questions.explain: Everyone has feelings, even though we like different things.

questions.q: What makes you special?
hints: Think about your name and face.
Is there another child exactly like you?
questions.explain: There is only one you. That makes you special.

reflect.q: What do you like most about you?

units.parent: Your child talked about what makes them special and how people are different. Ask them what new thing they learned to do this week.
units.teacher: Shows whether the child names their own abilities and accepts differences between people.
units.done: You are special, and so is everyone else.

units.subject: Identity and Belonging
units.title: Taking turns and sharing
units.caps: National Curriculum Framework for Children from Birth to Four (2015), Early Learning and Development Area 2: Identity and Belonging (children build strong relationships; take turns, share and follow simple rules)
units.intention: Today I am learning how to take turns and share.
units.prompt: How did you feel when you waited?

lesson.say: Taking turns means one person goes, then the next person goes. Everyone gets a chance.
lesson.html:
🧒 ➡️ 👧 ➡️ 🧒

Taking turns means one person goes, then the next. Everyone gets a chance.

lesson.say: Sharing means letting others use things too. We can share toys, crayons and snacks.
lesson.html:
🧸 🖍️ 🍊

Sharing means letting others use things too.

lesson.say: Waiting can be hard. You can take a deep breath and count to five while you wait.
lesson.html:
😮‍💨 1 2 3 4 5

Waiting can be hard. Take a deep breath and count to five.

example.q: Two children want the same swing. What can they do?
steps: One child swings first. Then the other child has a turn.

questions.q: Your friend has no crayons. What can you do?
hints: Your friend wants to draw too.
You can let your friend use some.
questions.explain: Sharing your crayons means you can both draw.

questions.q: It is not your turn on the slide. What do you do?
hints: Your turn will come if you wait.
questions.explain: We wait in the line. Our turn will come.

questions.q: What can help you while you wait?
hints: Something that helps you feel calm.
questions.explain: Breathing and counting help us feel calm while we wait.

questions.q: Nomsa shared her orange with you. What do you say?
hints: What do we say when someone is kind?
questions.explain: We say thank you when someone shares with us.

questions.q: Why do we take turns?
hints: Would it be fair if only one child played?
questions.explain: Taking turns is fair. Everyone gets a chance to play.

units.parent: Your child practised ideas about sharing, taking turns and waiting calmly.
units.teacher: Shows whether the child can choose prosocial responses and a calming strategy for waiting.
units.done: When we share and take turns, everyone can play.

units.subject: Communication
units.title: Listen to the sounds
units.caps: National Curriculum Framework for Children from Birth to Four (2015), Early Learning and Development Area 3: Communication (children listen to sounds and speech; identify a wide range of sounds; enjoy songs and rhymes)
units.intention: Today I am learning to listen carefully.

lesson.say: We hear sounds with our ears. Some sounds are loud and some are soft.
lesson.html:
👂 🔊 🔈

We hear sounds with our ears. Some sounds are loud and some are soft.

lesson.say: A cow says moo. A dog says woof. A cat says meow. A duck says quack.
lesson.html:
🐄 🐕 🐈 🦆

A cow says moo. A dog says woof. A cat says meow. A duck says quack.

lesson.say: Listen. Can you hear a car, a bird or people talking?
lesson.html:
🚗 🐦 🗣️

Close your eyes and listen. What sounds can you hear around you?

steps: A dog says woof and a cat says meow.

questions.q: Which animal says woof?
questions.explain: A dog says woof.

questions.q: Which animal says quack?
questions.explain: A duck says quack.

questions.q: Which one makes a loud sound?
questions.explain: A drum makes a loud sound. A feather is very quiet.

questions.q: What do we hear with?
questions.explain: We hear with our ears.

questions.q: A baby is sleeping. How should we talk?
hints: We do not want to wake the baby.
questions.explain: We talk softly so the baby can sleep.

units.parent: Your child listened for animal sounds and loud and soft sounds. Try a listening walk together.
units.teacher: Shows whether the child matches sounds to sources and distinguishes loud from soft.
units.done: Good listeners hear so many sounds.

units.subject: Communication
units.title: Pictures tell a story
units.caps: National Curriculum Framework for Children from Birth to Four (2015), Early Learning and Development Area 3: Communication (children make meaning by "reading" what they see; arrange pictures to form a story)
units.intention: Today I am learning to tell a story from pictures.

lesson.say: A story has a beginning, a middle and an end. First, next, last.
lesson.html:
1️⃣ 2️⃣ 3️⃣

A story happens in order: first, next, last.

lesson.say: First, we plant a seed. Next, it gets water and sun. Last, a flower grows.
lesson.html:
🌰 ➡️ 💧☀️ ➡️ 🌻

First we plant a seed. Next it gets water and sun. Last a flower grows.

lesson.say: Pictures can tell us what is happening, even before we can read words.
lesson.html:
📖 👀

Pictures can tell us what is happening, even before we can read the words.

example.q: A boy is getting ready for bed. What comes first: brushing teeth or sleeping?
steps: We brush our teeth before we get into bed.
First we brush our teeth. Last we sleep.

questions.q: Put the seed story in order.
hints: The seed needs water to grow.
questions.explain: Plant, water, then a flower grows.

questions.q: Put the egg story in order.
questions.explain: First an egg, next it cracks, last a chick comes out.

questions.q: What comes last when we eat a banana?
options: Put the peel in the bin
hints: The peel goes in the bin last.
questions.explain: We peel, eat, and last we put the peel in the bin.

questions.q: Put the morning in order.
hints: What happens when you are still in bed?
You get dressed before you go out.
questions.explain: Wake up, get dressed, then go to school.

questions.q: What helps us know what a story is about?
questions.explain: Pictures help us know what is happening in a story.

reflect.q: What helped you put things in order?

units.parent: Your child put picture stories in order using first, next and last. Ask them to tell you about their day in order.
units.teacher: Shows whether the child sequences familiar events and uses first, next and last.
units.done: First, next, last. Now you can tell a story.

units.subject: Exploring Mathematics
units.title: Counting to 5
units.caps: National Curriculum Framework for Children from Birth to Four (2015), Early Learning and Development Area 4: Exploring Mathematics (children count and use number names in play)
units.intention: Today I am learning to count to 5.

lesson.say: One, two, three, four, five. We say one number for each thing we count.
lesson.html:
1 2 3 4 5

One, two, three, four, five. We say one number for each thing.

lesson.say: Touch each apple as you count. One, two, three. There are 3 apples.
lesson.html:
🍎 🍎 🍎

Touch each apple as you count: one, two, three. There are 3 apples.

lesson.h: The last number tells how many
lesson.say: When we count 4 ducks, the last number we say is 4. So there are 4 ducks.
lesson.html:
🦆 🦆 🦆 🦆

The last number we say tells us how many. There are 4 ducks.

example.q: There are two balls on the grass. How many balls?
steps: Touch the first ball and say one.
Touch the next ball and say two.

questions.q: How many stars?
questions.explain: One, two, three. There are 3 stars.

questions.q: How many fish?
hints: Say one number for each fish.
questions.explain: There are 5 fish.

questions.q: How many cars?
questions.explain: There is 1 car.

questions.q: Which number comes after 3?
questions.html: 1→2→3→?
questions.explain: One, two, three, four. 4 comes after 3.

questions.q: Which has more?
questions.explain: 4 biscuits is more than 2 biscuits.

units.parent: Your child counted groups up to 5. Count stairs, spoons or shoes together at home.
units.teacher: Shows one-to-one correspondence and whether the child knows the last count gives the total.
units.done: You can count to 5. Count things all around you!

units.subject: Exploring Mathematics
units.title: Circles, squares and triangles
units.caps: National Curriculum Framework for Children from Birth to Four (2015), Early Learning and Development Area 4: Exploring Mathematics (shapes and space; sorting by colour, size and shape)
units.intention: Today I am learning the names of shapes.
units.prompt: How did you know which shape it was?

lesson.say: A circle is round. It has no corners. A plate and a wheel are circles.
lesson.html:
⚪ 🍽️ 🛞

A circle is round. It has no corners.

lesson.say: A square has 4 sides that are all the same. A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.
lesson.html:
🟥 🔺

A square has 4 sides, all the same. A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.

lesson.say: We can sort things into groups. We can sort by shape, by colour or by size.
lesson.html:
🔴🔴 🔵🔵

We can sort things into groups by shape, colour or size.

example.q: A slice of watermelon has 3 sides. What shape is it like?

questions.q: Which shape is round?
hints: A square and a triangle have corners.
questions.explain: A circle is round with no corners.

questions.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
questions.explain: A triangle has 3 sides.

questions.q: Which is shaped like a circle?
questions.explain: A wheel is round like a circle.

questions.q: Sort by colour.
questions.explain: Red ball and red apple go together. Blue car and blue cup go together.

questions.q: Which is bigger?
hints: Think about how big they are.
questions.explain: An elephant is much bigger than a mouse.

units.parent: Your child named circles, squares and triangles and sorted by colour. Go on a shape hunt in your home.
units.teacher: Shows whether the child names basic 2-D shapes by features and sorts by one attribute.
units.done: Shapes are everywhere. Look for circles, squares and triangles!

units.subject: Creativity
units.title: Colours all around
units.caps: National Curriculum Framework for Children from Birth to Four (2015), Early Learning and Development Area 5: Creativity (children explore art materials, colour and making things)
units.intention: Today I am learning about colours.

lesson.say: Red, yellow, blue and green. Colours are all around us.
lesson.html:
🟥 🟨 🟦 🟩

Red, yellow, blue and green. Colours are all around us.

lesson.say: When we mix yellow and blue paint, we get green. Red and yellow make orange.
lesson.html:
🟨 + 🟦 = 🟩

🟥 + 🟨 = 🟧

Mixing paint makes new colours.

lesson.say: The sky is blue. Grass is green. The sun looks yellow.
lesson.html:
🌤️ 🌿 🍊

The sky is blue. Grass is green. An orange is orange!

example.q: Lindiwe mixes red and yellow paint. What colour does she get?

questions.q: What colour is grass?
questions.explain: Grass is green.

questions.q: Yellow and blue make…
questions.explain: Yellow and blue make green.

questions.q: What colour is a banana?
hints: It is the same colour as the sun in pictures.
questions.explain: A ripe banana is yellow.

questions.q: Red and yellow make…
hints: Like the colour of an orange.
questions.explain: Red and yellow make orange.

questions.q: What colour is the sky on a sunny day?
hints: Look up on a sunny day.
It is not the colour of soil.
questions.explain: On a sunny day the sky is blue.

reflect.q: What would you like to paint?

units.parent: Your child named colours and learned that mixing colours makes new ones.
units.teacher: Shows colour naming and early understanding of colour mixing.
units.done: You can make new colours by mixing!

units.subject: Creativity
units.title: Loud and soft, fast and slow
units.caps: National Curriculum Framework for Children from Birth to Four (2015), Early Learning and Development Area 5: Creativity (children explore music, rhythm and movement)
units.intention: Today I am learning about music and moving.
units.prompt: How does the music make you want to move?

lesson.say: Music can be loud, like a big drum. Music can be soft, like a whisper.
lesson.html:
🥁 🔊 🤫 🔈

Music can be loud or soft.

lesson.say: Music can be fast, like a running cheetah, or slow, like a tortoise.
lesson.html:
🐆 💨 🐢

Music can be fast or slow.

lesson.say: When music is fast, we can move fast. When music is slow, we can move slowly.
lesson.html:
💃 🕺

We can move our bodies to music: fast, slow, big and small.

example.q: The music is slow and soft. How can you move?
steps: You can sway slowly, like a tree in a soft wind.

questions.q: Which animal is fast?
questions.explain: A cheetah is fast.

questions.q: Which sound is soft?
questions.explain: A whisper is soft.

questions.q: The music is fast. How do you move?
hints: Match your body to the music.
questions.explain: Fast music, fast moves!

questions.q: Which can make music?
hints: Which one makes a sound when you tap it?
A sock is soft and quiet.
questions.explain: A drum makes music when you tap it.

questions.q: A tortoise is…
hints: Think of how a tortoise walks.
questions.explain: A tortoise is slow.

units.parent: Your child explored loud and soft, fast and slow in music. Dance together to different songs.
units.teacher: Shows whether the child distinguishes dynamics and tempo and links them to movement.
units.done: Music can be loud, soft, fast or slow. Keep moving!

units.subject: Knowledge and Understanding of the World
units.title: Animals and their babies
units.caps: National Curriculum Framework for Children from Birth to Four (2015), Early Learning and Development Area 6: Knowledge and Understanding of the World (children explore living things around them)
units.intention: Today I am learning about animals and their babies.
units.prompt: What did you notice about the baby animals?

lesson.say: Animals have babies. A baby cat is a kitten. A baby dog is a puppy.
lesson.html:
🐈 🐱 🐕 🐶

A baby cat is a kitten. A baby dog is a puppy.

lesson.say: A baby cow is a calf. A baby sheep is a lamb. A baby chicken is a chick.
lesson.html:
🐄 🐑 🐔 🐣

A baby cow is a calf. A baby sheep is a lamb. A baby chicken is a chick.

lesson.say: Animals need food, water and a safe place, just like we do.
lesson.html:
🥣 💧 🏠

Animals need food, water and a safe place.

example.q: What is a baby chicken called?
steps: A baby comes out of the egg.

questions.q: What is a baby dog called?
hints: A kitten is a baby cat.
A baby dog is a puppy.
questions.explain: A baby dog is a puppy.

questions.q: What is a baby cat called?
hints: A lamb is a baby sheep.
A baby cat is a kitten.
questions.explain: A baby cat is a kitten.

questions.q: Who is the lamb's mother?
hints: A lamb's mother is a sheep.
questions.explain: A lamb is a baby sheep.

questions.q: What do all animals need?
questions.explain: All animals need water to live.

questions.q: What comes out of an egg?
hints: Puppies are born from their mother dog.
A chick comes out of an egg.
questions.explain: A chick hatches out of an egg.

reflect.q: Which baby animal do you like?

units.parent: Your child matched animals to their babies and talked about what animals need.
units.teacher: Shows vocabulary for young animals and awareness of basic needs of living things.
units.done: Baby animals grow up, just like you.

units.subject: Knowledge and Understanding of the World
units.title: Sunny, rainy, windy
units.caps: National Curriculum Framework for Children from Birth to Four (2015), Early Learning and Development Area 6: Knowledge and Understanding of the World (children explore the weather and their environment)
units.intention: Today I am learning about the weather.
units.prompt: What is the weather like today?

lesson.say: The weather can be sunny, rainy, windy or cold.
lesson.html:
☀️ 🌧️ 💨 ❄️

The weather can be sunny, rainy, windy or cold.

lesson.say: When it is sunny, we wear a hat. When it rains, we wear a raincoat. When it is cold, we wear a jersey.
lesson.html:
👒 🧥 🧶

Sunny: a hat. Rainy: a raincoat. Cold: a warm jersey.

lesson.say: Grey clouds can bring rain. A blue sky means it may be sunny.
lesson.html:
☁️ 🌧️ 🌤️

Grey clouds can bring rain. A blue sky may mean sun.

example.q: It is raining. What should Kabelo take outside?

questions.q: It is sunny and hot. What do you wear?
hints: Scarves and gloves keep us warm.
A hat keeps the sun off your face.
questions.explain: A sun hat protects us from the sun.

questions.q: What keeps you dry in the rain?
hints: What do you hold above your head?
questions.explain: An umbrella keeps the rain off.

questions.q: The trees are moving and a hat blows away. What weather is it?
hints: We cannot see it, but we feel it.
questions.explain: The wind moves the trees and blows hats away.

questions.q: It is very cold. What do you wear?
hints: Cold means we need to be warm.
A costume is for swimming on hot days.
questions.explain: A warm jersey keeps us warm on a cold day.

questions.q: What can grey clouds bring?
hints: Look at the sky before it rains.
The clouds go dark and grey.
questions.explain: Grey clouds often bring rain.

units.parent: Your child talked about weather and what to wear. Look at the sky together each morning.
units.teacher: Shows weather vocabulary and the link between weather and clothing choices.
units.done: Look at the sky every day to see the weather.

words: tiny living things that can make us sick
